title: Evan Christopher and the decline of Bourbon Street jazz clubs
summary: Evan Christopher speaks out; Player moved to New Orleans in 1994 and notes few jazz clubs remain on Bourbon Street.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: I do know Evan. He’s very outspoken about it.
Yeah. I’ve been reading some of his things about music and the service industry and all that.

Yeah, he’s very outspoken about it, and rightly so. Because it’s a struggle. I mean if you can think of like I mean this is even really before I moved — I moved to New Orleans in ’94. In the 70’s or something, when all the clubs on Bourbon Street were basically jazz clubs. Now on Bourbon Street there are two jazz clubs. And yeah, two jazz clubs. And there’s one of the, Preservation Hall, or at least clubs that are supposed to be playing traditional jazz clubs or Dixieland or whatever you want to call it. So I mean that says a lot, all those, it’s gone. So now you’ve got karaoke clubs and cover bands and blues clubs, but maybe a lot of that is because that’s what our society now would rather pay to hear, for their entertainment, than it was in the 70’s, when there was more people listening to jazz.
